meta.title: Pressure Washing in Roseville, MI | HD Landscape
meta.description: Older concrete walks, patios and pavers in Roseville, MI washed with a wide, low spray by HD Landscape, based next door. Free itemized estimates.

hero.title: Decades of grime. **Easy on the joints.**
hero.lede: Many Roseville homes date to the 1950s and 1960s, so their walks and patios have often seen decades of weather on damp clay ground. HD Landscape cleans them with a wide, low spray and says plainly what will and will not come off.

local.title: What decades outside do to a Roseville walk or patio.
local.intro: More than half of the homes here were built in the 1950s and 1960s, and the city is now entirely built out. So most walks and patios here have years of foot traffic and winter grit behind them. A good wash brings back a lot of that. It will not bring back all of it, and we would rather say so before you hire us.

points.title: Old concrete has limits
points.body: A wash takes off grime and green growth. It will not fix concrete that is already pitted or worn, and too much pressure can leave marks. A small test spot shows how much the surface can take and what to expect from the rest.

points.title: Damp ground grows green
points.body: USDA soil maps rate nearly all of Roseville somewhat poorly drained or worse. Where paving stays damp and shady, moss and algae move in. If a patio keeps going green, look at the downspout and the grade, because [yard grading](/yard-grading/) may do more than another wash.

points.title: Pavers behind older homes
points.body: A paver patio added behind an older house may have been losing joint sand for years, and a wash shows how far it has gone. A small drop may need a top up, weedy joints may call for [polymeric sand](/polymeric-sand/), and anything rocking or sunken is a base problem. Jake can say which one you have.

points.title: Between tenants or before a sale
points.body: About one home in three here is rented, and a clean walk and patio are the first thing a new tenant or buyer sees. A wash is a simple job to fit in between one and the next, and it pairs well with a [cleanup](/spring-and-fall-cleanups/).

logistics.title: A clean Roseville walk shows what the joints need.
body: We are based next door in St. Clair Shores, so this is close to home for us. Jake looks at the surface and the stains, then writes a free itemized estimate with a straight answer on what should come off and what may not.

A careful wash clears the surface first and sorts out where the water will run, because storm drains lead straight to local water. Then it is a small test spot, a wide spray at a low angle and a clean water rinse. Once it dries, the joints show whether they need sand.

faq.q: Do you do pressure washing in Roseville, MI?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape pressure washes walks, patios and pavers in Roseville, and we are based next door in St. Clair Shores. For another surface, including a driveway, text a photo to [(586) 718-8762](tel:+15867188762) and Jake can say whether we can take it on.

faq.q: Can you make my old concrete patio look new?
faq.a: Cleaner, yes. New, no. Washing takes off grime and green growth, but stains that have soaked in and concrete that is pitted or worn stay that way. A patio that has sat out in Roseville since the 1950s has earned some of its marks. A small test spot is the way to see what yours will do before the rest gets washed.

faq.q: Why does the shady side of my patio turn green so fast?
faq.a: Because it stays wet. Much of Roseville sits on clay soils that drain slowly, and paving in the shade does not get a chance to dry out. Moss and algae settle in. Washing removes them, but they return if the spot stays damp, so look for a downspout or low spot that is feeding it.

faq.q: Should I pressure wash before listing or renting out a house?
faq.a: It helps, and it is a small job to fit in. On a street of Roseville homes from the 1950s and 1960s, a clean walk is one of the quickest ways to make a house look cared for. Tell us your date and we will see what works. Pair it with a [spring or fall cleanup](/spring-and-fall-cleanups/) and the whole front of the house gets the same treatment.

faq.q: Should I sand my pavers before or after pressure washing?
faq.a: After. Wash first, let everything dry, then fill the joints. Doing it the other way can lift fresh joints back out. On Roseville's damp ground a shaded patio can take longer to dry, so give it the time. See [polymeric sand](/polymeric-sand/) for how that part works.
